title: Product overview, PRD, design spec, roadmap, pricing & release notes - Dec 2026
author: Sofia Martinez
body:
Summary:
This consolidated product document summarizes Redwood Inference's product direction for inference runtime, the related PRD and acceptance criteria, high-level design decisions, the roadmap and themes for 2026 Q1–Q4, pricing and packaging guidance for hosted and dedicated tiers, and the December 2026 release notes. The goal is to provide a single-reference artifact for engineering, product, sales, and customer success when planning rollouts and customer conversations.

1) Product overview (one-paragraph):
Redwood provides a unified inference platform that offers Hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, and Private deployments with consistent API semantics and production-grade SLAs. This document focuses on improving model selection automation, reducing per-token inference cost by 15% for typical workloads, and expanding Dedicated autoscale controls for multi-tenant pools.

2) Goals and success metrics (2026):
- Business goals:
  - Increase hosted API revenue by 35% YoY through higher retention and feature-led expansion.
  - Grow Dedicated committed capacity ARR by 50% via simplified packaging and self-serve reservations.
- Product/technical goals:
  - Reduce median token latency for common generation workloads by 20% across the hosted fleet (target median < 80ms for 2k-token context on x1 GPUs).
  - Reduce average cost-per-token by 15% through smarter batching, KV caching, and quantization profiles.
  - Ship model-selection automation (Model Router) v1 with canary rollout to 20% of traffic.
- Success metrics (KPIs):
  - Latency SLO: 95th percentile request latency < 350ms for gen endpoints (seq len 2048).
  - Cost metric: Average cost-per-1K tokens for the top-10 customers reduced by >=15% vs baseline (2025 Q4).
  - Adoption: 50 customers on Dedicated autoscale within 6 months of GA.

3) Scope and non-goals:
- In scope:
  - Model Router v1: policy-driven selection between model variants (accuracy/cost/latency).
  - Autoscale controls for Dedicated pools with policy UI and API.
  - Pricing tiers update for Dedicated and Hosted tokens (see pricing section).
- Out of scope for this release:
  - Full multi-cloud private control plane (planned for 2027).
  - New model training features.

4) PRD (requirements) - must-have, should-have, nice-to-have:
- Must-have:
  - MR-001: Model Router API (POST /v1/model-router/route) that returns selected model id and metadata.
  - MR-002: Server-side canary: ability to route X% of traffic to a new model variant (configurable).
  - AS-001: Dedicated autoscale policies: min/max VGPU, scale-in/out based on p95 latency and queue depth.
  - SLO-001: Observability hooks exposed to Redwood Console with per-route latency and cost buckets.
  - SEC-001: Audit logs for routing decisions and policy changes (retention 90 days).
- Should-have:
  - MR-003: Offline simulation mode to run policy decisions on historical traffic.
  - AS-002: Burst capacity option with pre-warming (configurable minutes).
  - DOC-001: Customer-facing rollout guide and API examples.
- Nice-to-have:
  - MR-004: Multi-objective optimizer for routing (latency + quality + cost).
  - AS-003: Predictive autoscaling using short-term traffic forecasting.

Acceptance criteria (examples):
- Given a new model variant and 10% canary config, within 5 minutes rollback must be possible via Console or API with a single click/POST.
- Dedicated autoscale policy: when p95 latency exceeds threshold for 3 consecutive minutes, system should scale up within 2 minutes and restore within 5 minutes after load subsides.

5) Design spec (high-level, decisions and diagrams):
- Components:
  - Control Plane: Model Router Service (MRS), Policy Manager, Audit Logger.
  - Data Plane: Serving Runtime (existing), Autoscaler, Pre-warm pool manager.
  - Console: Policy editor, metrics dashboard, canary control.
- Key design decisions:
  - Decision 1: Keep model selection as a control-plane-only decision to avoid per-request cold-paths. The MRS returns the model id and hints; the data plane caches decisions to avoid RTTs. Rationale: prevents added latency and allows centralized rollout control.
  - Decision 2: Autoscale signals will be multi-sourced (p95 latency, queue depth, GPU utilization). Use weighted scoring to avoid noisy single-metric flips.
  - Decision 3: Audit logs are written to the same immutable event store used by infra (s3-parquet + Glue catalog) and indexed for 90-day lookups in Console.

- Traffic flow (text diagram):
  1. Client -> Redwood API (route request)
  2. API checks local model mapping cache; if stale or miss -> calls Model Router Service
  3. Model Router returns model_id + exec_profile + confidence score
  4. Request routed to Serving Runtime using model_id; runtime applies KV cache and batching
  5. Metrics and audit events emitted to metrics pipeline and event store

- Caching details:
  - Local model mapping cache TTL: 60s (configurable)
  - KV cache: per-customer prefix caching with size limit 8GB per pool
  - Batch window targets: 10–50ms depending on latency class

- API examples (curl):
  $ curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/model-router/route \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${API_KEY}' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"customer_id":"cust_123","request_profile":{"seq_len":1024,"latency_budget_ms":150}}'

  Example response (JSON payload):
  {"model_id":"rwd-llama-70b-q5b","exec_profile":"fast","confidence":"0.82","recommendation":"serve","reason":"cost-latency tradeoff"}

6) Roadmap & themes (2026):
- Q1 2026:
  - Ship Model Router v1 (control plane + cache) + public API beta.
  - Launch Dedicated autoscale policy alpha with 5 pilot customers.
- Q2 2026:
  - Console policy editor GA (UI + API parity).
  - Pricing pilot: new Reserved Dedicated Bronze/Silver/Gold tiers.
  - Begin Model Router offline simulation tool.
- Q3 2026:
  - Burst capacity and pre-warm pool GA.
  - Model Router canary rollout automation (auto-rollout based on safety metrics).
- Q4 2026:
  - Multi-objective routing experiments, 20% traffic on autopilot.
  - Pricing and packaging iteration post-pilot; scale Dedicated sales motion.

Cross-cutting themes (impacting roadmap):
- Observability-first: every rollout must expose per-segment metrics and anomaly detectors.
- Cost transparency: surfaced per-route cost-to-serve in Console and Billing.
- Reliability & rollback: automatic fallback to prior model variant on quality regressions.

7) Pricing & packaging notes (guidance for GTM / sales):
- Hosted API (text gen) - updated pricing (effective 2026-06-01):
  - Standard: $0.003 / 1K tokens (baseline GPU-backed small models)
  - Large-model tier: $0.009 / 1K tokens (verifies performance profile)
  - Embeddings: $0.0008 / embedding (128-d equivalent)
- Dedicated reserved capacity - new packaging (trial pricing shown):
  - Bronze: 1–4 VGPU reserved, best-effort autoscale, $X/month baseline (sales to calculate region-specific margins).
  - Silver: 5–16 VGPU reserved, guaranteed throughput 80% of capacity, $Y/month.
  - Gold: 17+ VGPU reserved, SLA-backed latency targets, priority burst access, $Z/month.
- Add-ons:
  - Observability retention: extra 90/365-day tiers for per-route metrics.
  - Compliance package: SOC2 + extra audit logs retention (12 months) priced per customer.
- Discounting guidance:
  - Do not exceed 30% total discount without VP approval.
  - Multi-year commitments have step-down pricing after year 1 with a minimum 12-month commitment.

8) Release notes (December 2026 release):
- Release name: Model Router + Dedicated Autoscale v1 (2026-12-01)
- Summary of changes:
  - New: Model Router Service (MRS) v1 with public API and Console integration.
  - New: Dedicated autoscale policies with p95 latency and queue-depth signals.
  - Improved: Serving runtime batching defaults optimized for common seq-len distributions, estimated cost savings 12% on average.
  - Fixed: Several edge-case failures when KV cache invalidation coincided with model rollouts.
- Notable bug fixes:
  - Fixed an issue causing delayed metrics ingestion for models with high concurrent KV cache evictions (ENG-1427).
  - Addressed race in pre-warm pool allocation causing temporary over-provisioning (ENG-1499).
- Known issues:
  - In rare conditions (high churn models) the model mapping cache TTL may cause a short-lived increased latency spike. Mitigation: reduce TTL to 15s for high-change customers via support toggle.

9) Rollout plan and runbook (operational steps):
- Canary rollout steps (Model Router v1):
  1. Create model variant and register in Model Catalog (owner: Applied ML).
  2. Configure 5% canary traffic in Policy Manager (owner: Eng Platform).
  3. Monitor key metrics for 60 minutes: per-route latency, error rate, quality regression score (eval set).
  4. If metrics stable -> increase to 20% for 2 hours.
  5. If at any point metric degradation > threshold (error-rate + latency + quality) -> rollback to previous variant and trigger postmortem.
- Rollback criteria (thresholds):
  - Error rate increase > 0.5% absolute over baseline for 5 consecutive minutes.
  - p95 latency increase > 25% over baseline for 10 minutes.
  - Quality regression: BLEU/ROUGE/LLM-specific eval drop > 3% on regression suite.

Runbook snippets:
- Quick rollback command (API):
  $ curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/model-router/rollback \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${API_KEY}' \
    -d '{"policy_id":"policy_abc","reason":"auto-rollback-threshold"}'

11) Appendix - examples, configs, and links:
- Autoscale sample policy (YAML):
  name: default-dedicated-policy
  min_vgpu: 2
  max_vgpu: 32
  signals:
    - name: p95_latency_ms
      operator: '>'
      threshold: 300
      weight: 0.6
    - name: queue_depth
      operator: '>'
      threshold: 50
      weight: 0.3
    - name: gpu_utilization
      operator: '>'
      threshold: 0.85
      weight: 0.1

- Example telemetry query (PromQL):
  avg_over_time(request_duration_ms{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])

- Owner should review this doc quarterly or when major roadmap shifts occur.
- For proposed changes to pricing or SLOs, include stakeholders in a RFC PRD and route for sign-off (product -> eng -> sales -> finance).

If you have questions or need a shorter overview for customers or sales, contact the product owner (sofia.martinez@redwood.com).
